blocking.section: Context and problem statement (line 19); Decision drivers (line 29); Decision outcome (line 43); Pros and cons of the options > Native Kafka wire-protocol proxying (line 141)
blocking.issue: The ADR treats a per-message Route as what P7 requires and rejects wire proxying for 'breaking P7'. The vision document defines P7 differently: a session maps to the request Phases, and each message maps to `onChunk`. The owning document says per-message routing through the request Phases is a P7 exception and leaves it open in OQ-multi-protocol-18. That open question's option (b), a session Route with each message as `onChunk`, is the shape that conforms to P7. The ADR therefore contradicts a foundation document (vision P7) and the owning document's Topic ingress section. It also never cites OQ-multi-protocol-18, which is the open question this decision depends on.
blocking.evidence: Line 19: "Each message stays inside the Route, Policy and Filter Chain model (P7)". Line 29: "- **One Filter Chain (P7)**: each message needs a Route; record batches seen by a wire proxy do not have one." Line 43: "and mediation keeps every message on a Route." Line 141: "its Phases see record batches with no per-message Route, breaking P7." Vision, Principles: "| P7 | Protocols are native | Every protocol maps onto the same `Route`, `Policy` and Filter Chain model through a documented Phase mapping: a session maps to the request Phases, each message to `onChunk`". Owning document, Topic ingress: "Each message is a request on the Route whose `match.topic` matches, headers as headers and value as body, running the request Phases (a P7 exception: OQ-multi-protocol-18)."
blocking.fix: Line 19: replace "(P7)" with "(a P7 exception pending OQ-multi-protocol-18)". Line 29: replace the driver with "- **Per-message governance (P7 exception, OQ-multi-protocol-18)**: publish, topic ingress and embedded PUBLISH run each message through the request Phases of a Route; a wire proxy sees record batches with no per-message Route or Consumer." Line 43: write "mediation keeps every message on a Route (a P7 exception, OQ-multi-protocol-18)". Line 141: replace "breaking P7" with "so records would reach Policies only as `onChunk` under P7, where `authz.*`, `ratelimit` and `quota` do not run".

blocking.issue: The ADR limits `ProducerLinger(0)` to Routes that await the acknowledgment. The owning document applies it to every Node without condition, and every publish Route answers 202 only after the acknowledgment. An acknowledgment mode is only a proposed option in OQ-multi-protocol-8. The conditional wording implies Routes that do not wait for the acknowledgment. That contradicts the owning document, which the ADR must agree with. It also treats a franz-go client option as a Route setting.
blocking.evidence: Line 47: "`ProducerLinger(0)` on Routes that await it, since v1.20.0 made the default linger 10 ms". Owning document, Publishing from HTTP: "franz-go's default linger became 10 ms in v1.20.0, so Nodes set `ProducerLinger(0)`" and "The Node answers 202 once the broker acknowledges". OQ-multi-protocol-8 lists "acknowledgment mode" as an open `messaging` option.
blocking.fix: Replace the clause with "`ProducerLinger(0)` on every franz-go producer client, since every publish Route awaits the acknowledgment (an acknowledgment mode is OQ-multi-protocol-8)". This agrees with the owning document and still satisfies the catalog's "on Routes that await the acknowledgment".

foundation_amendments: Vision P7 maps 'a session ... to the request Phases, each message to `onChunk`'. Multi-protocol topic ingress, embedded PUBLISH and this ADR instead route each message through the request Phases of a `match.topic` Route. The owning document's Native wire-proxy stance also says, without qualification, that mediation keeps every message 'inside the Route and Filter Chain model (P7)'. Close OQ-multi-protocol-18 so that P7 means one thing: either amend P7 and pack section 4 to record the per-message exception, or adopt its option (b).
